source.title: MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers
source.authors: Róbert Csordás; K. Irie; Jürgen Schmidhuber; Christopher Potts; Christopher D. Manning

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares parameter-matched Transformer architectures and evaluates downstream scores across model sizes, but does not fit or test scaling-law equations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out perplexity comparisons between parameter-matched MoEUT and dense Transformers, and zero-shot downstream scores across sizes. It does not fit power laws, test extrapolation from small runs, vary the parameter/token allocation at fixed compute, or assess whether compute-optimal allocations follow a trend. Figure 4 also compares performance against training MACs, but reports no fitted exponents or separately stated numeric curve values.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture-proposal paper. It compares its own MoEUT model with parameter-matched dense, σ-MoE and SUT baselines and ablates its own design choices. It fits no power laws and tests no extrapolation, allocation or predictive downstream relation. Kaplan et al. is cited only for the observation that shared-layer Transformers are not compute-efficient. MoEUT versus dense is a change of model family (MoE plus layer sharing), not the depth/width/shape variation at fixed parameters that V4 names. The layer-grouping and layernorm ablations are internal design choices of MoEUT. Downstream averages rising with size are reported without any predictive fit, so they do not bear on V6's 'predictably' either. All rows are the study's own method compared with others or its own ablations.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim more strongly that MoEUT outperforms parameter-matched dense baselines from 44M to 1B on C4, SlimPajama, peS2o and The Stack, and does so using significantly less compute. They also claim it beats dense models by a large margin at equal training MACs. Downstream differences are described as marginal. They make no scaling-law claims and leave massive scaling to future work.
record.recipe_differences: This is an architecture-comparison study, not a reproduction of the scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation methods. Models use a fixed 100k-step training protocol and selected parameter-matched comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture choices matter in the reported ablations: layer-group size and ordering affect perplexity, and PeriLN outperforms PreLN and PostLN, with the normalization gap described as larger for smaller models.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched parameter count (44M–1B), MoEUT changes held-out perplexity relative to dense pre-LN Transformers by about 0.3–5% (e.g., 18.97 to 18.30 at 44M, 11.15 to 10.90 at 1040M on C4). Its internal grouping and layernorm choices also shift perplexity, with AABB ordering 'almost as bad as not doing grouping'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameter count, changing architecture family (shared-layer MoE versus dense) shifts loss only modestly, while within-family design choices can matter more.

record.problems: The authors describe the training regime as modest and say massive scaling remains future work. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Several architecture-ablation values are available only in figures; the text gives qualitative descriptions rather than exact values. Downstream rows here use the study's aggregate averages, not each individual benchmark score.
record.rows_left_out: Individual downstream task scores in Table 1 and Table 2 are not separately extracted; aggregate task averages were retained to represent the across-size downstream trend. Figure 4's training-MAC comparison is noted in gate_note but not rowed because it presents curve-level comparisons without separately stated numeric values by model and compute setting.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss in parameters, tokens or compute; Fig. 4 plots perplexity against parameters and MACs over about 1.4 orders of magnitude only.
Fixed 100k steps for all sizes; no compute-optimal sweep.
No depth/width/aspect-ratio variation of a dense model at fixed parameters.
The Stack code runs are compared with a baseline only; no scaling form is tested.
No predictive relation between downstream scores and scale or loss.
No fitting choices or exponents compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V4/V6 labels should be dropped. The study evaluates its own architecture against baselines and does not test any version of the scaling-law claim. Fig. 4 curves (perplexity against parameters and against training MACs) have no fit or stated values.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test power-law form, several-orders coverage, or independent parameter, token, and compute scaling.
No small-run fit or prediction of substantially larger-run loss.
No compute-budget sweep that selects loss-minimizing parameter and token counts.
Tests selected MoEUT-versus-dense architecture comparisons and selected layer-grouping and normalization variants, not a broad range of depth and width choices.
No tests of the same power-law form in other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer. Code training is evaluated, but no scaling-law form is tested there.
Reports downstream aggregate scores at selected sizes; does not fit a predictive relation between task performance and scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitted exponents or allocation laws under alternative fitting choices, nor test curves bending away from a power law.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Parameter-matched MoEUT and dense Transformer comparisons on C4, peS2o, and SlimPajama
reader_labels.reason: Their reported perplexities are generally close, with MoEUT slightly lower in these comparisons; see R01–R22.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Layer grouping and layer ordering in the 244M C4 model
reader_labels.reason: The study reports G=2 as optimal and says AABB ordering is significantly worse than alternating grouping, so architecture choices are not uniformly negligible; see R34–R40.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: PeriLN consistently performs best, with a more significant gap for smaller models; exact figure values are not stated, so the magnitude cannot be assessed; see R41–R46.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MoEUT aggregate downstream scores across tested sizes and training datasets
reader_labels.reason: The reported task-average scores rise with parameter count for each dataset series; see R23–R33.
